speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You have presented with increasing pain and swelling in your left knee for the past two months. To begin our evaluation, can you describe the nature of the pain and whether it is constant or comes and goes?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is concerning since the pain is severe enough to wake you from sleep and hasn't responded to ibuprofen. Do you notice any redness, warmth, or a visible lump on the left knee?

speaker: Measurement
text:
RESULTS: 
CBC: Within normal limits

Knee X-Ray: A lytic lesion in the distal femur near the knee joint with a thin rim of bone on the external surface and a 'soap bubble' appearance.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Tumor of Bone.

The X-ray finding of a "soap bubble" lytic lesion in the distal femur is classic for this condition, which typically affects young adults. I will now request MRI images to confirm the extent of the lesion and check for soft tissue involvement.
